reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and scheme pages 25–52, with general notes on pages 1–2. Every printed part reconciled to detailed allocations; all final question/solution crops inspected before publication.
sourceNotes: All ten questions retained: 45 tasks and 380 offered marks. Exam-level choice does not remove practice questions. Q4(a)(i)–(ii) share 20D; Q9(c)(i)–(ii) also share 20D.

The Q9 summary erroneously lists an extra 10C for (c)(i), which would total 60 marks. The detailed joint 20D allocation and its criteria cover both the table and expectation, consistent with the paper’s 50 marks. The summary also mislabels (d) as (d)(iii).
The Paper 2 scale table on page 26 is incorrectly headed Paper 1. Its 15C is (0,5,10,15) and 20D is (0,6,12,17,20), distinct from Paper 1. Preserve these Paper 2 bands.
Q2(b) prints 4k=8 but the preceding equation gives 4k=−8. Its final centre (5,−2) and radius 3 are correct.
Q3(b) retains the labelled angle diagram and all justifications. Q3(d) retains both valid alternative routes, each with a 5D tariff, without adding their marks.
Q4(a)(i) stops after the cofunction identities without the final substitution. An attributed NextStepUni supplement completes the proof; part (ii) and the joint allocation remain attached.
Q5(c) says A and B are independent, but it is C and D in this question. The working and final probability 0.7 use C and D correctly.

Q7(a)(iv) uses the rounded AB=29.9 from the previous part. Keeping AB=16+8√3 until the end also rounds to a cylinder height of 5 cm. Q7(a)(vi) duplicates the same absolute-value branch; the other sign would put the centre outside the prism. Its final circle is correct.

Q8(b)(i) gives 11:00 for the interval after both cars have passed O. If B’s constant motion is also assumed before it passes O, 100t=|120t−40| gives an earlier equal-distance time t=2/11 hour after 9:00. The printed question does not expressly exclude that interval. Keep the official answer with its assumption explicit.
Q8(b)(iii) prints the discarded negative root as −23/115; the printed factors give −23/155. The valid time remains 9:36.
Q9(a) uses a weighted sum of class midpoints, Σxf=1380. Q9(d) stops at male:female=3:2; the requested proportion is male/(male+female)=3/5=60%. An attributed worked example completes this answer.
Q10(a)(iii) has the wrong intermediate logarithmic inequality: n ln(0.92)≤ln(0.1), then dividing by a negative number reverses it. Its final minimum n=28 is correct.
Q10(b)(i) uses z rounded to −0.83; Q10(b)(ii) reuses the rounded 20%. Unrounded normal probabilities give the same requested final answers: 20% and 10.12 ml.

Q10(c) correctly finds z≈−1.57, but accept H0 / mean has not changed overstates the result. An attributed supplement states fail to reject H0: insufficient evidence of a change at 5%, not proof of no change. All original criteria remain visible.

cards.stem: A company produces eye drops. The eye drops are sold in small bottles. The amount of liquid in the bottles follows a normal distribution with mean 10 ml and standard deviation 0·18 ml.
cards.questionText: The machine used by the company to fill the bottles is serviced and adjusted. The company want to check if the mean amount of liquid in the bottles is still 10 ml. They take a random sample of 50 bottles and find the mean amount of liquid is 9·96 ml. Carry out a hypothesis test at the 5% level of significance to see if this shows a change in the mean amount of liquid in the bottles. State clearly your null hypothesis, your alternative hypothesis, your conclusion, and a reason for your conclusion.
cards.markingNote: At z≈−1.57, fail to reject H0 at 5%: there is insufficient evidence of a change. This does not prove that the mean has stayed at 10 ml. The original wording overstates the conclusion; NextStepUni supplies the precise interpretation.
